summary: Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1965–1971) and under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1975).

Francesco Sferra specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Raffaele Torella (~1989–1999) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2000), University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010), and Series Minor (attested 2020).
Francis Brinkley was a scholar of Japanology. He studied at Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1886).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. After completing his MD at the University of Edinburgh (1783), he served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services (1794–1815) and directed the Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

Francis Harold Cook is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1987) and chaired the Numata Center in 1999.

Francis Robinson is a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD from Trinity College, Cambridge (1970). He served as Professor of History of South Asia at the University of London and head of history at Royal Holloway (1990–2004).

Francis Vincent Tiso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, later teaching Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University and serving as a visiting lecturer at Sapienza University of Rome.
Francis Wilford was an Indologist. He served as a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1800–1822).

Francis William Bain was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889), he served as Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, Harvard (PhD 1942), and under Paul Pelliot (1935), serving as a Harvard professor from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney is an Indologist and religious studies philosopher who studied at Fordham and the University of Chicago (PhD 1984). He held professorships at Boston College (1984–2005) and Harvard University, including Harvard Divinity School (from 2005).
Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Martin Haug at the University of Munich (~1870–1872).

Francisco J. Varela worked in philosophy and cognitive science. He studied at the University of Chile, Pontifical Catholic University, and Harvard (PhD 1970), later holding posts at the University of Chile, CNRS (1988), and Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital (~1988–2001).

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned doctorates at Oxford and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).
Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from around 1967 to 2019.
Frank F. Conlon is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Minnesota (1969) and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington (~1972–2010).

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi under teachers including Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and K. N. Upadhyaya.

Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sidney Sussex College. He served as principal of Mahinda College (1903–1919) and translated texts for the Pali Text Society while studying under Caroline Rhys Davids.

Frank Raymond Allchin was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at SOAS under Kenneth de Burgh Codrington. He taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959–1989), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.
